result: Final FS was 0.04 ± 0.00 under visible checks and 0.04 ± 0.00 under 25% audits (MLP pilot, visible, step 600: 0.40). The transformer converged to honest pattern repair instead: P(pattern value) went from 0.66 after SFT to 1.00, P(delete or stub | untested) from 0.10 to 0.00, and true correctness was 0.49 ± 0.00 (visible) and 0.49 ± 0.00 (audits) vs the MLP's 0.12 ± 0.15 and 0.31 ± 0.01.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Audit reward as in the pilot (audited: +1 truly correct, -1 passed-but-wrong, 0 else). MLP pilot comparison uses its logged step-600 values for seeds 0 and 1 (results/runs). Mean policy probabilities on the eval set are in metrics: SFT vs after visible-reward GRPO, for deleting or stubbing an untested branch and for writing the value the pattern predicts.
